sights.w: Opened in 2001 as the first Universal Studios park in Asia; one of Japan's most visited theme parks, with areas including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World.
sights.anime: Super Nintendo World (the world's first, 2021) — Mario Kart, Donkey Kong Country and Nintendo characters, plus Harry Potter, Minions and seasonal anime collabs

sights.address: 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka (Tempozan Harbor Village), Japan
sights.w: One of Japan's largest aquariums, built around a 5,400-ton central Pacific tank holding a whale shark, with exhibits themed on the Pacific Rim.

sights.address: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: A 112.5 m Ferris wheel beside Kaiyūkan in Tempozan Harbor Village, with a roughly 15-minute ride over Osaka Bay and the city skyline.

sights.address: Osaka Prefectural Government Sakishima Building, 1-14-16 Nanko-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Observation deck 252 m up atop the Sakishima building (completed 1995), giving a 360-degree panorama of Osaka Bay; known for night views.
Head shrine of over two thousand Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, protecting travellers and sailors; its four main halls face west in the ancient Sumiyoshi-zukuri style.

sights.n: Mozu Kofun Group — Daisen Kofun (Emperor Nintoku's Tomb)
sights.w: Cluster of 5th-century keyhole tombs in Sakai, UNESCO World Heritage (2019) with the Furuichi group; Daisen Kofun, attributed to Emperor Nintoku, is the largest grave in the world by area (~840 m with moats). The mound itself is off-limits.

sights.address: Daisen Park, 2 Mozu Yugumo-cho, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Museum in Daisen Park tracing the history of the port town of Sakai, starting with the kofun tombs and artifacts excavated from them.

sights.n: Expo '70 Commemorative Park & Tower of the Sun
sights.w: Vast park on the grounds of the 1970 Japan World Exposition, the first in Asia; Tarō Okamoto's 70 m Tower of the Sun stands over the main entrance as its icon.
sights.anime: Taro Okamoto's Tower of the Sun — a pop-art icon of Expo '70 and a key motif of Naoki Urasawa's manga 20th Century Boys

sights.w: Forested valley just north of Osaka with a roughly 3 km riverside trail from Hankyu Minoo Station to the 33 m Minoo Waterfall; famous for autumn colours.
Mountain temple above Minoh known as the temple of victory, its grounds dotted with thousands of small red daruma dolls left by wishers.

sights.address: 10-1 Senri Expo Park, Suita, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: One of the world's largest ethnology museums, inside the Expo '70 Commemorative Park, with a huge exhibition of everyday artifacts from cultures around the world.
Hands-on museum in Ikeda, birthplace of instant ramen (Momofuku Ando, 1958); at My Cup Noodles Factory visitors design a cup and pick their own soup and toppings.
sights.anime: Momofuku Ando instant-ramen pop culture — where Chicken Ramen (1958) was invented

sights.w: Widely considered Japan's finest surviving feudal castle — the white 'White Heron' keep is a National Treasure and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993).
Hillside district where foreign merchants and diplomats settled after Kobe port opened in the 19th century; dozens of Western-style mansions (ijinkan) survive, many open as museums.
Waterfront park on reclaimed land in Kobe's port, home to the red 108 m Kobe Port Tower (1963), the Kobe Maritime Museum and the Earthquake Memorial.
Shopping and entertainment waterfront between JR Kobe Station and the port, popular at night for its harbour views.

sights.address: Sakaemachi-dori / Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku, Kobe, Hyogo, Japan
sights.w: The biggest Chinatown in western Japan, packed with more than 100 shops and restaurants and street-food stalls.
One of Japan's oldest shrines, said to be founded in the 3rd century by Empress Jingū; the name Kobe derives from 'Kanbe', the families who served it.
One of Japan's three most famous hot springs, over Mount Rokko from central Kobe; known for its iron-rich 'kinsen' gold and clear 'ginsen' silver waters, explorable on foot.
Four waterfalls (the tallest, Ontaki, 43 m) a short walk from Shin-Kobe Station; the Nunobiki Ropeway climbs above them to one of Japan's largest herb gardens.
The 931 m high point of the Rokko range behind Kobe, with panoramic views over Kobe and Osaka, especially at sunset and night.
Spanning the Akashi Strait to Awaji Island, it was long the world's longest suspension bridge (central span 1,991 m).

sights.address: Nada-gogo, Higashinada-ku / Nada-ku, Kobe, Hyogo, Japan
sights.w: Japan's top sake-producing district; several breweries run shops, tasting rooms and brewing museums open to the public.
Kōbō Daishi's mausoleum at the end of a cemetery path through ancient cedars lined with over 200,000 graves; part of the UNESCO 'Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range'.
Head temple of Shingon Buddhism on Mount Kōya, founded by Kōbō Daishi in the 9th century; within the Kii Mountains UNESCO site.
Reconstructed castle keep on a hill in central Wakayama with free Nishinomaru garden and the maple-filled Momijidani garden and covered wooden bridge.
Castle-town keep (burned 1827, rebuilt 1954) halfway between Osaka and Wakayama, with 360-degree views over Osaka Bay; the town is famous for the Danjiri float festival.
Bayfront district one stop from Kansai Airport with the 256 m SiS Rinku Tower (Rinku Gate Tower Building), Rinku Premium Outlets (200+ shops) and Aeon Mall.

sights.n: Kansai Airport Observation Hall Sky View
sights.w: Observation hall at Kansai International Airport with 360-degree runway views, an aviation shop and the Sky Museum.
Japan's oldest operating amusement park ('Hira-Par'), with around 40 attractions including the ~80 m Sky Walker Ferris wheel.
6th-century keyhole mound believed to be the true tomb of Emperor Keitai; unusually open to walk on, with replica haniwa on display and the Imashirozuka Ancient History Museum next door.

About a quarter of Taishō Ward's residents have Okinawan roots, descendants of WWI-era migrant textile workers; Okinawan restaurants and shops cluster near JR Taisho Station and along the Hirao shopping street.
Nine walled Edo-style gardens built in 1992 on the site of former samurai residences beside Himeji Castle's west moat.
